skill.name: instagram-content-research
skill.description: Search Instagram posts by keyword through SocialDataX to collect samples for topic research, competitor comparisons, and content planning.
skill.summary: Find Instagram post samples and separate visible evidence from research conclusions.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: Most backtick alerts are Markdown formatting. The documented workflow runs an unpinned npm package that can read an API key from the environment or a credential file. No evidence of credential exfiltration or audit-targeted prompt injection was found in the supplied files.

remediation.issue: The CLI workflow runs a moving npm release with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and verify its integrity before execution. Require approval before downloading or running it in a credential-bearing environment.

remediation.issue: The CLI can read a persistent API key or select an unexpected credential source.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a managed secret store with a scoped key. Document legacy variable precedence and provide a way to revoke or remove saved credentials.

remediation.issue: The shell example does not require safe handling of dynamic search arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Pass keywords and continuation tokens as separate arguments with shell interpretation disabled, or use the structured MCP tool.

remediation.issue: Error-provided billing links are preferred without an explicit validation step.
remediation.suggestion: Always show the fixed SocialDataX billing URL. Require user confirmation before resuming a paid request and preserve the original page and item limits.

content.value_statement: It takes time to find relevant Instagram posts and compare them consistently. This skill uses SocialDataX search to collect traceable samples and summarize recurring content angles.
actual_capabilities: Search for Instagram posts by keyword using the SocialDataX CLI or a configured MCP connection.
Collect one page or set page and item limits for a larger search.
Merge multiple result pages and continue the same search with a returned continuation token.
Record available post titles, authors, links, IDs, metrics, and publication dates.
Separate observed evidence from interpretations and suggest follow-up questions.
Retain partial results and report which searches did not complete.
limitations: Requires working SocialDataX authentication. The documented CLI uses Node.js and npm, while MCP needs a configured connection.
Search results do not cover all of Instagram and cannot establish a trend by themselves.
The workflow does not log in to Instagram, publish posts, change accounts, or read local browser data.
Post fields can be missing, and service errors or low credit balances can interrupt collection.

use_cases.title: Find ideas for a new post
use_cases.description: Review a small keyword sample and note formats worth testing in your own content.

use_cases.title: Compare competitor messaging
use_cases.description: Search for two brands and compare the themes visible in bounded samples, with post references for review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a content planning brief
use_cases.description: Gather samples for a campaign topic and separate repeated angles from questions that need more evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Review one search page
prompt_templates.scenario: Explore a topic with a small sample.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the authorized SocialDataX connection to search Instagram for [topic]. Review one page and list up to three relevant posts with links or IDs.

prompt_templates.title: Identify recurring formats
prompt_templates.scenario: Collect examples for a content plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Instagram for [topic], with a limit of two pages or 20 posts. Group the sample by format and cite a post for each observation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two brands
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare search samples under the same limits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for [brand A] and [brand B] separately using the same page and item limits. Compare visible themes, cite examples, and flag missing evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Build a paginated research brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Track evidence across several pages without exceeding a fixed budget.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [keyword] with a total limit of three pages or 30 posts. Report partial results and confirm before resuming a paid request. Separate supported observations from hypotheses and cite the relevant samples.

output_examples.input: Review one page of Instagram results for balcony herb gardens.
output: Illustrative sample: Two posts show growing setups for small balconies.
Observation: One uses a railing planter, and the other groups pots by available sunlight.
Follow-up: Search for shade-tolerant herbs to see whether the same formats recur.

output_examples.input: Compare two fictional outdoor brands using one page of results for each.
output: Illustrative sample: A Ridge Field post shows a rainwear demonstration. A Trail Loom post shows a packing checklist.
Interpretation: The first example explains a product feature, while the second helps readers plan a trip.
Limit: These examples do not establish either brand's overall strategy.

output_examples.input: Collect up to three pages of posts about commuter cycling and report any interruption.
output: Illustrative result: The search returned eight posts from one page before it stopped because of a service error.
Partial observation: The available posts include gear checklists and route videos.
Status: The remaining pages were not collected. Confirm before resuming a paid request.

best_practices: Start with a focused keyword and one page, then expand only when the sample does not answer the question.
Use an authorized connection and omit confidential client names or campaign details from search queries.
Keep post links or IDs with observations and label incomplete results.
anti_patterns: Treating a keyword sample as proof of an Instagram-wide trend.
Pasting API keys into chat, commands, reports, or logs.
Automatically restarting a partial search from the first page and repeating requests.

faq.question: What input does the skill need?
faq.answer: Provide a keyword or topic. To compare brands or accounts, use their names as search terms.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: The CLI needs a SocialDataX key. An authenticated hosted MCP connection can use its existing credentials.

faq.question: Does the skill sign in to Instagram or interact with posts?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow searches for posts without signing in to Instagram, publishing, liking, commenting, or changing an account.

faq.question: Can I retrieve every matching post?
faq.answer: No. Search has no stable complete result set. Use page or item limits to define the sample.

faq.question: What happens if a page is empty or a search stops early?
faq.answer: An empty page does not prove the search is finished. Keep any partial results and use a valid continuation token within the original limits.

faq.question: Can searches use paid credits?
faq.answer: Yes. A search can stop when credits are insufficient. Review billing directly with SocialDataX before approving further paid requests.
